chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Ibn Fazzal, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He used to say during an illness.
O Allah! You have criticized certain people, saying: 'Say: Call upon those whom you claim (to be gods) besides Him, so they will not have the power to remove the distress from you nor to change it.'
So, O the One besides Whom no one else has the power to remove my distress or change it,
Send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad,
Remove my distress and transfer it to those who call upon another god alongside You.
There is no god other than You.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the supplication for illness that asks to transfer distress to those who call upon other gods?
ai.summary: This supplication, recorded in al-Kafi, exemplifies the Shia tradition of 'tawassul' through the attributes of God, specifically invoking the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt as a means to seek relief from illness. It creatively adapts the Quranic critique of false deities in Surah Al-Isra to transfer the supplicant's specific distress to those who worship idols, thereby affirming God's exclusive power to remove harm. This practice highlights the theological principle that while God is the ultimate source of healing, the Prophet and Imams serve as intercessors and channels of divine grace.
